Q: How to merge branch to trunk automatically A:

The command in your question is wrong because it has invalid parameters.

First, you need to ensure that your branch is in sync with trunk. See SVN MergeBook | Keep your feature branch in sync with trunk and SVNBook | Keeping a branch in sync.

Then you need to reintegrate your branch into trunk as described in SVN MergeBook | Merge (reintegrate) your feature branch into trunk and SVNBook | Reintegrating a branch.

Check the merging best practices in SVN MergeBook.

Steps for reintegrating a branch into trunk are as follows:

  1. Check out your trunk and cd into this working copy (or switch your existing working copy to trunk).
  2. Run the svn merge ^/branches/mybranchname/ command. You need to replace the path to your branch with an actual path from your repository.
  3. Examine the result of your merge and commit it if all is fine.

Note that all this can be done through TortoiseSVN's UI. The option is called "Merge a range of revisions" and can be usually done in a Next-Next-Finish manner. See TortoiseSVN Manual | Merging.

Q: Image feature extraction and reproduction A:

...The results I’m getting are not similar to those in my set of low-brightness images. I’d like to know what strategy can I should adopt to achieve a similar reproduction.

You need to show (or link) to some images files of type: .jpg or .png. Not a text-based web page.
If possible, edit them to be side-by-side. You must show two inputs and one output image.
You can add images by editing your question.

"I have a set of low-brightness images, and I want to reproduce the same characteristics (low brightness) using existing bright images."

Most likely you want Histogram Matching. Research that topic to see if it's a good option.

Q: what does setting a seed inside or outside a loop do when simulating a model? A:

The answer to this depends on why you are setting a seed in the first place. Setting a seed is useful for debugging and creating exactly reproducible examples. If you are concerned debugging your entire code or reproducing your entire data.frame, setting a single seed at the start should be enough. If you are worried that you might need to debug or reproduce a single iteration, setting a seed at the start of that iteration is better.

For your reasoning of 'keeping everything the same', though, setting a seed is inappropriate. The random seed shouldn't affect the statistics you are computing in any meaningful way, since they are controlling the random effects.

Q: How do I use this __something__ and what does it do? A:

In general, the reference for this is https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html

Note that some of them can behave in quite subtle ways and the details are often undocumented (e.g. a normally-declared __new__ is automatically made a staticmethod for Python classes, but is a pre-bound native method for C classes; if mutating it in place you must be careful).

There are also a few not listed there because they are library-only conventions (e.g. used by pydoc), or else are highly specific to some particular type.

See also https://docs.python.org/3/library/operator.html
